name: Singapore

sources.label: CPF Board — Who is exempt from CPF

taxRules.label: Income tax
taxRules.note: The full 13-step resident ladder, not an approximation. Reliefs (earned income, course fees, and so on) are not modelled, so this reads slightly high.

healthNote: Employment Pass employers are required to provide medical insurance, so the premium is usually theirs. Out-of-pocket sits in the health basket category.
notes: CPF does not apply to foreigners on an Employment Pass. The published 20% employee rate is the citizen and permanent resident figure — it is the single most common way this jurisdiction gets modelled wrong. You self-fund retirement out of take-home pay.
No joint filing. Singapore taxes individuals, so the filing status control is suppressed for this city.

colBasket.label: Housing
colBasket.note: Expat condo rent. Dominates the basket and moves fastest — replace it with a real listing.

colBasket.label: Eating out and drinks
colBasket.note: Hawker food is cheap; alcohol is heavily taxed. The average hides a wide spread.

colBasket.label: Transport
colBasket.note: Assumes no car. A COE makes car ownership a different category of decision entirely.

colBasket.label: Childcare and education
colBasket.note: International school fees are not in this figure and would dwarf it.
